title: Horae: ad usum Romanum (Rome)
imprint: Paris : Ulrich Gering and Berthold Rembolt, 16 Dec. 1494
subject: liturgy
general_notes: Created by A. Panzanelli and A. Rais.
physical_description_note:
On vellum. Rubricated. Each line of text between red rules. Woodcuts heavily coloured. Part of the small woodcut at the head of Mayus-Iunius has been cut away. At the end are bound 27 additional leaves of vellum, bearing a 'Cursus de passione Christi' and a 'Cursus pro defunctis in manuscript'. On 1a is the signature of Johan Wilhelm Zur Madten, Altrath [of Solothurn?], 1657, in the top the armorial book-plate of Urs. Hos. Nic. Louis Glutz de Blozheim [of Solothurn], conseiller d'état, cy-dev. officier au service de Sardaigne, and on a fly-leaf the signature of Conrad Gluz von Blozheim, canonicus in Solothurn. At the foot of 1b is written: Ex dono D.ae B. n.tae B. a. 1781. Old black morocco (BMC).
The manuscript bound at the end mainly contents the two texts (Cursus de Passione Christi and a Cursus pro defunctis) written in 15th century bastard. Later, on the last leaf a list of saints has been added in a very different handwriting (antiqua in the shape used in the 18th century), listing many modern saints including several Jesuits.
Manuscript notes are mainly in German; there are also in French and Latin; e.g. on v8r three hands, four sentence, two in German, one in Latin (Deliberandum est diu, quod statuendum est semel) one in French (Fay bien Laysser dire). The portion of woodcut cut off on b4 is likely evidence of censorship, as the image represented the twins (the Gemini) naked.
